title: When the Oath Sings Again
premise: Yara Crane, a scribe bound by debt to the silent temple of the valley, is tasked with recording the arrival of a child who speaks a language older than any kingdom — a tongue that turns out to be the binding-contract of souls sold to the court beneath the mountain. When Yara discovers her own grandmother's name in that ledger, she realizes her family's survival was purchased with a soul now held as collateral, and the child is its living echo. Fleeing the valley where magic cannot follow, Yara and the child cross a wintering land of broken oaths and bargain-hungry courts to steal the soul back before the long winter seals the mountain for a generation. In the end, Yara must choose between erasing her family's debt and keeping the child — and she pays the price by surrendering her own name to the ledger, freeing both soul and child while becoming a story the mountain itself remembers.
about_author: Rafael Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging medieval oath-records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, promises, and the people trapped between them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes the debt-bound life: copying ledgers in a temple where magic cannot exist, counting days owed. A tremor in the silence hints something is coming. Emotional beat: quiet resentment masked as duty.

chapters.title: A Knock Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A child arrives at the temple door at dusk, speaking a language no one knows — except it appears unbidden on Yara's own page as she tries to transcribe it. The abbot orders the child locked away. Beat: fear mixed with fascination.

chapters.title: Ink That Moves
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, night scene. The child's words rewrite themselves into Yara's ledger, revealing a fragment: a name — Crane — listed among souls sold beneath the mountain. Yara recognizes her grandmother's handwriting beside it. Beat: vertigo of inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Abbot Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Yara and the child (rendered as impressionistic fragments). Confrontation with the abbot reveals the temple's purpose: it exists to keep such children out of the world's memory. He offers to erase the child's mind. Beat: betrayal by an institution.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She steals the original contract pages and flees with the child through the valley's edge — the boundary where magic dies. Crossing it, the child's language becomes audible song. Beat: first breath of freedom and terror.

chapters.title: The First Winter Road
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the road, they meet Merric, a disgraced oath-broker who recognizes the stolen pages and offers passage in exchange for a cut. Yara distrusts him but has no map. Beat: uneasy alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: Songs in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Child's POV, lyrical and strange. The child explains — through dream-images — what they are: the residue of a soul split from its owner, walking until someone claims or destroys them. Beat: heartbreak; the child knows what they are.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Promises
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A checkpoint where travelers pay with minor oaths. Merric advises lying; Yara instead pays with a true promise, weakening her position but earning the tollkeeper's warning: the court below already knows they travel. Beat: cost of honesty.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, flashback-heavy. Studying the contract, Yara reconstructs how her grandmother sold a soul to buy the family's survival during a famine — and why the debt passed down. Beat: grief curdling into anger at an ancestor she loved.

chapters.title: The City of Counted Days
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach a trade city where Merric's enemies find him; a chase through archive-streets ends with Merric captured and the pages nearly lost. Yara saves him against her judgment. Beat: loyalty tested by self-interest.

chapters.title: What Merric Confesses
chapters.summary: Merric's POV. He admits he was hired to retrieve the child for the court beneath the mountain — his freedom was the price. He chose, too late, not to complete it. Beat: guilt, and the theme of survival's price made explicit.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Snow falls out of season; the mountain court is sealing itself for a generation. They have days, not months. The child begins to fade as winter deepens. Beat: ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Frozen Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the mountain's gate, a herald demands payment: an oath of equal weight to the one being reclaimed. Yara offers her name; the herald accepts provisionally, marking her hand. Beat: dread dressed as formality.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The descent through the mountain's halls of recorded debts — shelves of souls filed like documents. The child grows stronger here, horrifyingly at home. Beat: awe inverted into horror.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Audience with the court's magistrates, beings of pure contract. They are courteous, legalistic, immovable: the soul was bought fairly. Yara argues inheritance law against them using her scribe's training. Beat: intellect as weapon.

chapters.title: The Loophole and the Trap
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara finds a flaw — the contract named a debtor dead three years before signing, voiding it — but the court counters by producing Merric's hire-contract, making him liable instead. Beat: victory snatched away; moral weight shifts.

chapters.title: Merric's Choice
chapters.summary: Merric's POV. Facing eternal service, Merric tears up his own contract, an act the court cannot undo without breaking its own laws — buying Yara one hour of chaos. Beat: redemption through self-destruction.

chapters.title: Stealing Back a Soul
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax part one. In the vault, Yara finds her grandmother's soul — aged, diminished — and the child's origin beside it. She can carry only one out before the hour ends. Beat: impossible choice crystallized.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax. Yara writes herself into the ledger in exchange for both — offering her name, her record, her remembered existence. The court accepts. She carries the soul and child out as the mountain seals behind them. Beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: After the Sealing
chapters.summary: Child's POV. Outside, winter breaks early. The child, whole now, carries Yara's forgotten name in their new memory — the only place it survives. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; inheritance reversed.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Was Not
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, unnamed and unrecognized even to herself, returning to the valley with the child and the freed soul. The temple records show no Yara Crane; her debt dissolved with her name. She chooses to stay anyway. Beat: freedom found inside loss.

chapters.title: When the Oath Sings Again
chapters.summary: Child's POV, closing. Years later, the child — grown, keeping the valley's new archive — reads aloud the story of a scribe who paid with her name, and somewhere in the telling, faintly, an oath sings. Beat: resolution; stories as the only true repayment.
